learn.hook: Two friends bring sweets to share. How many sweets now?
points: Adding means putting things together.
We use the plus sign + to add.
The equal sign = shows the answer.
Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller one.

example.q: Riya has 4 laddoos. Mummy gives her 3 more. How many now?

learn.reallife: We add when friends join a game or more sweets come to the plate.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎 and 🍎🍎. How many apples in all?
quiz.mistake: Counts one group only, or one extra

quiz.q: What is 4 + 4?
quiz.mistake: Writes the two numbers side by side

quiz.q: Arjun has 5 marbles. He finds 2 more. How many now?
6 children play cricket. 3 more join. How many play now?
What is 7 + 0?
quiz.explain: Adding 0 adds nothing. So it stays 7.

quiz.q: Meena has 2 red balloons and 6 blue ones. How many balloons?

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 berries. I find 2 more. How do I know how many I have?
teach.praise: Put them together and count on. 5 berries! Yum!
teach.nudge: Do I add or take away? How do I count them?

topics.title: Add and draw: family, fingers and toes

learn.hook: How many fingers and toes do you have? More than you think!
points: To show 3 + 2, draw 3 balls. Then draw 2 more. Count them all.
Count your family and a friend's family to find how many in all.
We have 10 fingers on our hands and 10 toes on our feet.
10 fingers and 10 toes make 20 in all.

example.q: Riya's family has 4 people. Aisha's family has 5. How many people in all?

learn.reallife: When two families meet for a festival, we add to know how many plates to lay out.

items.text: I drew 🎈🎈🎈, then 2 more. Now there are ___.
3 fingers up on one hand and 4 on the other show ___.

games.title: True or false?
items: To show 2 + 4, draw 2, then draw 4 more.
A family of 3 and a family of 3 make 9.

quiz.q: Kabir draws 4 stars. Then he draws 3 more. How many stars now?
Meena's family has 3 people. Joseph's family has 6. How many people in all?
How many fingers and toes do you have in all?
Aisha shows 5 fingers on one hand and 2 on the other. How many fingers?
How many toes are on your two feet?
quiz.explain: 5 toes on each foot. 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: Harpreet shows all the fingers of one hand and 4 of the other. How many fingers?
quiz.explain: A whole hand is 5. 5 and 4 make 9.

teach.ask: Gappu: Birds have no fingers! How many fingers and toes do you have altogether?
teach.nudge: How many fingers? How many toes? Now join them.

learn.hook: Roll, win and tick! Who will win the most rounds?
points: Two players roll a dice. The bigger number wins that round.
Put a tick ✓ on the scoreboard for each win.
At the end, count the ticks for each player.
The player with more ticks won more rounds.

example.q: Riya has ✓✓✓✓. Kabir has ✓✓. Who won more rounds? By how many?

learn.reallife: In cricket, the scoreboard shows runs. More runs means the team is ahead.

quiz.q: Meena's scoreboard shows ✓✓✓✓✓. How many rounds did she win?
Arjun has ✓✓✓. Joseph has ✓✓✓✓✓✓. Who won more rounds?
quiz.explain: Joseph has 6 ticks. Arjun has 3. 6 is more.

quiz.q: Riya has ✓✓✓✓. Aisha has ✓✓. How many more rounds did Riya win?
quiz.mistake: Adds the ticks instead of comparing

quiz.q: Kabir rolls ⚄. Harpreet rolls ⚂. Who gets a tick?
quiz.explain: ⚄ is 5. ⚂ is 3. 5 is bigger, so Kabir wins the round.

quiz.q: They played 7 rounds with no ties. Riya won 4. Kabir won the rest. How many did Kabir win?
quiz.mistake: Gives Kabir the same as Riya

quiz.q: What does one tick on the scoreboard show?
quiz.explain: We put one tick each time a player wins a round.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the tick stands for

teach.ask: Gappu: I have ✓✓✓ and my friend has ✓✓✓✓✓. Who won more?
teach.praise: 5 ticks beat 3 ticks. Your friend won more. Good game!
teach.nudge: How many ticks does each of us have?

learn.hook: Hop, hop, hop on the number strip! Where will you land?
points: Colour 3 beads red and 4 beads blue. Count all the beads: 7.
On a number strip, start at the first number.
Hop forward as many steps as the second number.
The number where you land is the sum.
learn.reallife: Hopscotch on the school ground is like hopping on a number strip.

quiz.q: Riya colours 3 beads red and 4 beads blue. How many beads in all?
Start at 6 on the number strip. Hop 2 forward. Where do you land?
quiz.mistake: Counts the start as a hop

quiz.q: How do you find 4 + 5 on a number strip?
quiz.explain: Start at the first number and hop the second number.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where to start

quiz.q: Kabir hops 3 and lands on 9. Where did he start?
Hop to find 2 + 7. Where do you land?
quiz.explain: Start at 2 and hop 7: you land on 9.

quiz.q: A mala has 5 green beads and 5 yellow beads. How many beads?

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 3 + 4 on the number strip?
teach.praise: Start at 3, hop 4, land on 7. Hop hop hooray!
teach.nudge: Where do I start? How many hops?

learn.hook: Kabir and Meena add in different ways. Can both be right?
points: Kabir counts all: 1, 2, 3, and so on. Meena counts on from the bigger number. Both get the same sum.
3 + 4 and 4 + 3 are both 7. The order does not change the sum.
A number can be made from two parts: 6 is 2 + 4, 3 + 3 or 5 + 1.
Match each sum with its answer, then check.

steps: Way 2: start at 6 and count on 2: 7, 8.

learn.reallife: Some friends add on fingers, some on beads. The answer stays the same!

quiz.q: Riya knows 5 + 2 = 7. What is 2 + 5?
quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the sum.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new order gives a new sum

quiz.q: Joseph counts all to find 3 + 5. Aisha counts on from 5. Who is right?
quiz.explain: Both ways give 8. Any correct way is fine.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one right way

quiz.q: Which pair makes 9?
quiz.mistake: Does not add the parts to check
Writes the whole instead of the part

quiz.q: Which is the same as 4 + 3?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 uses the same numbers, so it is also 7.
quiz.mistake: Changes the numbers, not just the order

quiz.q: Kabir has 8 marbles in two bags. One bag has 6. How many in the other?

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend says 2 + 7 = 9 and I say 7 + 2 = 9. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both right! Changing the order keeps the sum the same.
teach.nudge: Do 2 + 7 and 7 + 2 use the same numbers?

learn.hook: Is it a plus story or a minus story? Let us find out!
points: More coming? Then add with +.
Some going away? Then take away with -.
Adding makes the number bigger (but adding 0 keeps it the same).
Taking away makes the number smaller (but taking away 0 keeps it the same).

example.q: There are 4 cows. 3 more cows come. Add or take away?

learn.reallife: Guests arriving means add. Sweets eaten means take away.

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. Add or take away?
quiz.explain: More ducks come. So we add.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when more are coming

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. How many ducks now?
8 crayons are in a box. 3 fall out. How many are in the box?
quiz.explain: Some go away, so take away. 8 - 3 = 5.

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 5 + 2 or 5 - 2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks plus and minus give the same answer

quiz.q: 3 + ___ = 8. What is missing?
quiz.explain: Count on from 3 to 8: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 5.

quiz.q: Riya has 9 diyas. 4 blow out. How many still glow?
quiz.explain: Some go out, so take away. 9 - 4 = 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a story needs plus or minus?
teach.praise: More coming means add. Going away means take away. Smart!
teach.nudge: What do I do when more come? What about when some go away?

topics.title: Make an addition story; sum puzzle

learn.hook: Open your bag! Can you make a story that adds?
points: An addition story has two groups that join.
'I have 3 books. I put 2 more in my bag. Now I have 5.'
Sum puzzle: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.
To make every line add to 6, put 1, 2 and 3 once in each line.

example.q: A puzzle line has 1 and 2 filled in. Which number goes in the empty box so the line makes 6?

learn.reallife: At home: 'Mummy bought 4 apples and 2 bananas. That is 6 fruits.'

items.text: I have 2 pencils and 3 crayons. I have ___ things.

games.title: True or false?
items: 'I had 4 books. I got 2 more.' is an addition story.
A puzzle line with 2, 2 and 2 uses 1, 2, 3 once.
'3 birds flew away' is an addition story.

quiz.q: Meena's bag has 4 books and 3 notebooks. How many in all?
Which is an addition story?
options: I had 2 pens. Papa gave me 3 more.
I had 4 pens. I gave 1 away.
quiz.explain: Getting more means the groups join. We add.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up adding and taking away

quiz.q: A line has 2 and 3. Which number makes the line add to 6?
quiz.mistake: Repeats a number already in the line

quiz.q: What is 1 + 2 + 3?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the numbers

quiz.q: A line has 3 and 1. Which number completes it to make 6?
quiz.mistake: Repeats a number already in the line

quiz.q: Arjun's bag has 5 pencils and 4 erasers. How many things in his story?

teach.ask: Gappu: Can you tell me an addition story about things in your bag?
teach.praise: What a story! Two groups joined and you found the total.
teach.nudge: What two groups are in my story? How many in all?

learn.hook: Beep beep! At each stop, a child gets down. Who is left?
points: The school bus has 5 children. At each stop, 1 child gets down.
5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0: one fewer each time.
When nobody is left, there are 0 children.
Draw the things, cross out the ones taken away, count the rest. Write it: 5 - 2 = 3.

example.q: 6 children are on the bus. 1 gets down at each of 2 stops. How many are left?

learn.reallife: On the way home, the bus gets emptier at every stop.

games.title: Bus stops
games.prompt: Children on the bus, from the start to the end

quiz.q: 5 children are on the bus. 1 gets down. How many are left?
quiz.mistake: Adds the child instead of taking away

quiz.q: 4 children are on the bus. 1 gets down at each stop. After 4 stops, how many are left?
3 children. 1 gets down at the first stop and 1 at the next. How many are left?
Riya draws 6 kites and crosses out 2. How many kites are not crossed out?
Which sentence matches 7 balls with 3 crossed out?
Only 1 child is on the bus. She gets down. How many are left?
quiz.explain: 1 take away 1 leaves 0. The bus is empty.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bus can't be empty

teach.ask: Gappu: 3 chicks were on my back. One hopped off at each stop. How many are left after 3 stops?
teach.praise: 3, 2, 1, 0. Zero chicks left. My back is free!
teach.nudge: What number do we get when nobody is left?

learn.hook: Five birds sit on a wire. Two fly away. How many stay?
points: Subtracting means taking away.
We use the minus sign - to take away.
Count back to find what is left.
Taking away 0 leaves the same number.

example.q: Kabir has 8 grapes. He eats 3. How many are left?

learn.reallife: When we eat sweets, the plate has fewer. When friends leave, fewer play.

games.title: True or false?
items: Take away all 5. None are left.

quiz.q: 5 birds sit on a wire. 2 fly away. How many stay?
What is 9 - 3?
Aisha has 7 balloons. 4 pop. How many are left?
Joseph has 6 rotis. He eats all 6. How many are left?
quiz.explain: All are eaten. None are left. 6 - 6 = 0.

quiz.q: What is 8 - 0?
Harpreet has 9 stickers. She gives 5 to Riya. How many does she keep?

teach.ask: Gappu: I had 6 worms. I ate 2. How many are left? How do you know?
teach.praise: Count back from 6: 5, 4. Four left! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Do I take away or add? How do I count back?

learn.hook: A hand covers some dots! How many are hiding?
points: A card has 7 dots. A hand hides some. We see 4.
Hidden = all the dots take away the dots we see: 7 - 4 = 3.
Check by adding: 4 seen + 3 hidden = 7.
Adding and taking away are linked: 4 + 3 = 7, so 7 - 3 = 4.

example.q: 8 dots in all. 5 can be seen. How many are hidden?

learn.reallife: If you know 10 children are in a group and 7 are in the room, 3 must be outside.

quiz.q: A card has 6 dots. A paper hides some. You see 4. How many are hidden?
9 dots in all. 3 can be seen. How many are hidden?
Aisha has 7 shells. Some are under a cup. 2 are outside. How many are under the cup?

quiz.explain: If 5 and 3 make 8, then taking 3 from 8 leaves 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the link between + and -

quiz.q: Kabir sees 4 dots. He knows 4 more are hidden. How many dots in all?
Which fact goes with 2 + 5 = 7?
quiz.mistake: Picks a fact with a different whole

teach.ask: Gappu: My card has 9 dots. My wing hides some. I see 6. How many are hidden?
teach.nudge: How many in all? How many can I see?

learn.hook: Hop backwards on the number strip! Careful, little frog!
points: To find 9 - 3, start at 9 on the number strip.
Hop back 3: 8, 7, 6. Land on 6.
You can also count up from 3 to 9, or use your fingers.
Any way is fine if the answer is right. Check by adding: 6 + 3 = 9.
learn.reallife: Counting down for a rocket launch is like hopping back: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1!

games.title: True or false?
items: Hopping back makes the number bigger.
Going back gives a smaller number.

quiz.q: Start at 9. Hop back 3. Where do you land?
Find 8 - 5.
Meena counts up from 4 to 9 to find 9 - 4. How many hops does she make?
quiz.mistake: Counts the starting number as a hop

quiz.q: Joseph says 7 - 3 = 4. How can he check?
options: Add 4 + 3 and see if it is 7
quiz.mistake: Does not know adding checks taking away

quiz.q: Use the number strip. What is 10 - 6?
quiz.explain: Hop back 6 from 10: you land on 4.

quiz.q: Riya hops back 2 from 6. Kabir counts up from 2 to 6. What do they both get?

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 7 - 2 on the number strip?
teach.praise: Start at 7, hop back 2, land on 5. And 5 + 2 = 7 checks it!
teach.nudge: Do I hop forward or back? Where do I start?
